title: walk.rs parse_structure: text_body/html_body as Option<&mut Vec> is harder to follow than a wrapper type
description: walk.rs parse_structure uses Option<&'a mut Vec<String>> for text_body and html_body to model nullable JS arrays. The resulting borrow patterns (*html_body = None; if let Some(ref mut tb) = text_body) are verbose. Suggested rewrite: introduce a small wrapper enum (Active(Vec<String>) | Nullified) with push/drain methods. This makes the nullification state explicit and eliminates the Option<&mut Vec> reborrow dance. The algorithm becomes a direct translation of the RFC JS pseudocode.
close_reason: Evaluated BodyList<'a> wrapper approach. Net assessment: wrapper saves ~8-10 lines at call sites but requires ~15 lines for type definition + methods — code is slightly longer overall. The existing doc comment on parse_structure already explains Option<&mut Vec> in RFC terms. The hardest section (end-of-alternative cross-population) does not simplify proportionally. *html_body = None with RFC citation comments is already readable. Introducing an indirection type adds cognitive load for a new reader without paying for itself. All 7 walk.rs tests pass; baseline confirmed. No simpler alternative without correctness risk.
